newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity falls as West generation returns.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity falls as West generation returns.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading lower Monday as generation units returned to service in the U.S. West, increasing supply at a time of moderate demand in the Northwest, industry sources said.

As of 1220 EDT, July California Oregon Border (COB) was trading down $1.15 per megawatt hour (MWh) at $20.35 following trade at $20.25-$20.80, while August was down 81 cents at the day's low of $23.20 after trade as high as $23.50 per MWh.
July Palo Verde (PV) was down $1.45 at $32.45 following exchanges in a range of $32.40-33.00, while August was down $1.21 at the day's low of $33.85 following a move as high as $34.25 per MWh.

A number of fossil fueled generation units were returning to service in the U.S. West late last week, while the 1,112 megawatt (MW) WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state was tentatively set to restart midweek pending approval from the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC).
Also, Southern California Edison pushed back the restart of the 1,080 MW San Onofre 3 nuclear unit in San Clemente, Calif., to July 10 from late June for additional work.
The 750 MW unit 5 at the Four Corners, New Mexico, coal-fired plant may be shut most of this week after it tripped off-line last Wednesday due to a tube rupture.
The 300 MW unit 4 at the Reid Gardner coal-fired power plant near Las Vegas is operating, but will be shut later today for testing, a spokesman for Nevada Power Co, the plant's operator, said Monday.

The unit, which had been out of service since a boiler explosion on March 2, began to ramp up last week, but more testing of its turbine is needed, the spokesman said. Unit 4 could be down until Thursday, he noted.

Temperatures in the Northwest would average four to eight degrees Fahrenheit below normal today and Tuesday before returning to seasonal levels later this week, while those in the Southwest would run up to five degrees above normal Monday and tomorrow and climb two eight degrees above normal Wednesday through Friday.
As of 1220 EDT, July Henry Hub natural gas futures were trading up three cents at $2.265 per million British thermal units.

Separately, the Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC) committee last week recommended a the Pacific Intertie transmission system be derated from July 1-30 to 6,300 MW from the current limit of 7,200 MW.
The plan requires the approval of the WSCC board.
COB open interest for June 20 fell 462 to 6,936, while PV open interest fell 1,270 to 6,498, NYMEX said.
